method:
Two masks, both derived from the after build at a FIXED camera pose, fixed visual time (42000 ms) and fixed seed (82031), so before and after frames are pixel-comparable.
  covered   = pixels that change when the nuketown-mountain-backdrop group is DETACHED from the scene. Detaching is the only removal that survives a frame here; setting .visible=false is overwritten by a per-frame presentation pass.
  ridgeSurface = covered AND repainted between before and after, i.e. the subset where the ridge is the VISIBLE surface rather than sitting behind the forest ring. This is the honest ridge-against-sky measurement; the wider "covered" set is diluted by the identical forest pixels in front of the massif and understates the before ratio.
sky = the same pixels in the backdrop-detached frame. ratio = ridge / sky.
The ridge GEOMETRY is unchanged between the two builds (same seed, same radii, same heights); only vertex colours, the material and the ground skirt moved, so one mask is valid for both.
whyTheBeforeRunCannotMaskItself: In the before build the massif is not drawn by its own meshes at all. legacy-main re-batches the whole pass31-neighbourhood-life group in palette-lit mode long after this module adds itself to it; art-kit batchStaticMeshes then deletes every attribute outside {position, normal} - the vertex COLOUR attribute with it - and replaces the material with a flat white MeshLambertMaterial keyed on the source material colour (0xffffff for a vertexColors material). The visible massif is a merged white batch under pass31-neighbourhood-life-render-batches while nuketown-mountain-ridge et al sit at visible=false. That is why the before run self-reports a meaningless ~1.0 over a 4% noise mask, and it is the root cause this pass fixes (group.userData.dynamic = true).

corroboration.note: Direct region sample on the original diagnosis frame, no masking involved.

botsCleared: Both sets are captured with __ATOMIC_ACRES_DEBUG__.clearBots() called before any frame. The first cut of these captures shipped an after-grass frame with a red damage vignette across it - a bot had shot the player while the capture camera was detached - which made a pure colour re-key look like it had gone dry and olive.
